name: Azure MCP
tagline: Manage Microsoft Azure resources from your AI agent.
shortDescription: The official Azure MCP server. List resource groups, manage virtual machines, query SQL Database, deploy Azure Functions, inspect Application Insights, and manage storage accounts. Uses your standard Azure credentials.
longDescription:
## What it is

The Azure MCP server, maintained by Microsoft. Exposes the Azure ARM APIs as MCP tools: resource groups, virtual machines, storage accounts, SQL Database, Cosmos DB, Azure Functions, App Service, Application Insights, Key Vault, and more.

## Why we recommend it

It comes from Microsoft, so it follows Azure SDK best practices and has the right credential model (Azure AD / service principal). The auth is granular: you give the agent a service principal with only the roles it needs, and the agent inherits those boundaries. For Azure SQL specifically, this is the easiest way to let an agent run read-only queries against your prod database.

## When to use it

- Azure infra management from chat (start/stop VMs, check status)
- Azure SQL read-only queries for ad-hoc data questions
- Application Insights log queries
- Cost analysis via the Azure Billing API
installInstructions:
1. Create an Azure AD service principal: `az ad sp create --id <app-id> --display-name mcp-agent`
2. Grant it the roles you want the agent to have (e.g., Reader for safe read-only)
3. Set: `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`
4. `uvx azure-mcp`
pricingDetails: Free. The MCP server is open source. Azure API calls are billed per-request by Azure.
